title: Win-Key+<any-key> opens start menu when released in wrong order

status.label: Fix the unmatched Windows-key release after shortcut remapping
status.detail: A user reproduced the Start menu opening when Win is released before the mapped key in a Win+O URI remap on PowerToys 0.100.2; another issue confirms the same release-order symptom.

judgment.rationale: The original report says a Win-key shortcut can run its action but still opens Start if Win is released first. A commenter reproduced this on PowerToys 0.100.2 by mapping Win+O to open a URI, then releasing Win before O. Issue #38359 reports the same behavior and explicitly says it is the same issue; that issue is closed. Closed issue #12666 discusses key-up remapping as an enhancement but has a different configuration and does not resolve this reproduced shortcut-release bug.
evidence: The report says releasing Win before the mapped key opens the Start menu after a Win-key shortcut.
A July 29, 2026 commenter reproduced the problem on PowerToys 0.100.2 with Win+O opening a URI and Win released before O.
Closed issue #38359 reports the same start-menu-on-release-order behavior and a commenter says it is the same issue.
Closed issue #12666 documents a separate request to apply key remapping on key-up; no linked fix for the current behavior was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Fix release handling so a consumed Win-key remap does not leave Windows with an unmatched Win-key release that invokes Start.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current-version reproduction isolates a key-release-order bug: the mapped action executes, but releasing Win first still triggers the shell. The remap engine likely needs to track and suppress the original Win release after it has consumed the chord.

proposed_fixes.title: Suppress the shell action for a consumed Win-key shortcut
proposed_fixes.root_cause: When Win+key is remapped to an action and Win is released before the other key, the engine appears to let the original Win release reach Windows after consuming the shortcut, so Start opens unexpectedly.
plan: Trace shortcut recognition and key-up handling for Win+key actions, including Run Program and Open URI.
Track when the Win modifier belongs to a consumed remapped chord and suppress the corresponding shell-triggering release.
Ensure state is cleared on all key-up orders, cancellation, focus change, and remap disable.
Add regression tests for both release orders and for the original Win key used alone.
verification: Verify Win+O mapped to Open URI runs the action without opening Start when Win is released first.
Verify the same mapping works when O is released first.
Verify a standalone Win press still opens Start and no modifier state remains stuck.
Verify Run Program and other shortcut actions do not regress.

confidence.rationale: A current-version reproduction confirms the release-order trigger and unwanted shell action, but the exact input-event state transition still needs code-level confirmation.

issue_context.summary: Win-key shortcuts execute their mapped action but may also open Start when Win is released before the other chord key.
known_information: The original report describes the Start menu opening when Win is released first.
A user reproduced the issue on PowerToys 0.100.2 with Win+O mapped to Open URI.
Closed issue #38359 reports the same release-order behavior.
Issue #12666 is related to key-up remapping but is a separate enhancement request and does not establish a fix.
inferences: The remap engine may be forwarding an unmatched Win-key release after consuming the chord; this needs confirmation in the input path.
issue_context.analysis: The latest reproduction isolates key release order and shows the mapped action itself succeeds. Correctly suppressing the corresponding shell-triggering release is a focused fix candidate, with standalone Win behavior preserved.
initial_investigation: Read the original issue and all comments, including the current-version reproduction and the Run Program versus Open URI discussion.
Reviewed #38359 and #12666; #38359 has the same behavior, while #12666 is a separate closed key-up feature discussion.

information_gaps.information: Whether the shortcut handler forwards the original Win key-up event after consuming the mapped chord
information_gaps.why_needed: This confirms the proposed correction point and ensures the change does not suppress standalone Win behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce Win+O mapped to Open URI on current stable with both key release orders and trace the physical and injected Win key-up events.

reproduce.title: Test Win+O release order
setup: Map Win+O to Open URI using http://example.com.
steps: Repeat while releasing O before Win.
reproduce.expected_result: The URI opens and the Start menu does not appear for either release order; pressing Win alone still opens Start.

actions.label: Approve the Win-key release handling fix
